_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Zero again in ch. 16, a delirium chapter built almost entirely out of manner-clause comparisons (the stairs, the voices, the courteous man) that was drafted with several 'the way X' constructions and had every one of them rewritten to a plain 'as' clause or cut, same remedy as ch. 15. Demoting to rest as flagged last time — five of the last six chapters at zero or one. Leave this construction alone for a real stretch; the plain-'as' replacement is doing the work now. Ch. 17 (first Maria chapter, new POV) drafted with nine instances of this exact shape on a first pass and every one was rewritten to a plain 'as' clause before the chapter was finished — the rest period holds even under a brand-new narrating voice; don't let POV novelty be an excuse to re-open it early.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Seventh chapter running at zero, including ch. 16, where a vague placeholder noun would have been the easy way to gesture at everything delirium left unnamed and wasn't reached for even once. Safe to consider this one fully retired rather than merely resting. Eighth clean chapter now in ch. 17 — a first draft used 'a thing' twice (Maria's new voice reaching for the same vague filler) and both were replaced with 'something' or cut. Treat as fully retired across POVs, not just Lloyd's.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Seventh chapter running at zero. A draft pass of ch. 16 produced a near-miss ('is, I have come to understand, a different skill altogether') in the Ivet beat and it was cut back to a plain statement with no self-aware hedge. Stays on watch rather than retired, since the delirium register makes this one easy to slip back into. Ch. 17 (Maria, new POV) stayed clean of the general-rule shape, but see the new 'i-have-anaphora' entry below — her confessional voice reaches for 'I have [verb]' sentence openers constantly, and this aphorism pattern is the thing that habit could calcify into if a later chapter lets one of those openers run on into a stated general rule instead of a flat personal fact.

Ch. 16 at 19, same band held through a whole-chapter unreliable-narration experiment. Contrast partner rotated to its most minimal form yet: Lloyd's long, overlapping delirium sentences pulled up short by Maria's bare grounding words reaching him from outside the slide (cup. window. blanket. her own hand.) rather than by another character's combat calls or institutional paperwork. Ch. 17 (first Maria chapter) holds the same band at 22, and did rotate the contrast partner as flagged: her long, looping guilt-sentences get cut short by plain nursing fact ('I did that.' 'I have checked.') rather than by anyone's dialogue. Keep watching that the short side doesn't collapse into the new i-have-anaphora habit below instead of staying genuinely varied.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: Four chapters running at exactly one use (Maria's hand on his chest, 'the same as I had every single time since the chapel'). Settled, controlled background usage. Ch. 17 drops to zero — the first chapter not to reach for it at all — likely just the new POV finding its own shapes rather than a deliberate rest; worth checking whether it resumes at one in ch. 18 before reading anything into the dip.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running clean. Ch. 16 was the strongest possible temptation for this one — a whole chapter of Lloyd trying to manage facts he can't otherwise process, including the knot-cord count — and it still reached for arithmetic as a dry joke rather than filing language. Treat as effectively retired. Ch. 16 was also Lloyd's last chapter on the page for the whole of Act III: the POV has moved to Maria for ch. 17-25, and since this construction is defined around Lloyd's specific filing-and-accounting self-talk, it's dormant rather than tracked for the Maria chapters — pick it back up only if the narration returns to Lloyd.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running without it. Not reached for in ch. 16 either, despite several places (the buried memory, the cord) where a negated restatement would have been an easy shape to default to; still safe to use if it arises naturally, not a default. Seventh clean chapter in ch. 17, carrying the habit's absence across the Act III POV change.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: Four chapters clean now. A draft pass of ch. 16's opening produced one bare trailing 'which told me...' close and it was split into two short declaratives instead, same remedy as ch. 12-13. Treat any return to the bare trailing-'which' shape as a real lapse. Ch. 17's first draft produced two more (Edie's visit, the prayer paragraph) and both were split into separate declarative sentences before the chapter was finished, same remedy again — this is clearly the construction Maria's looping, qualifying sentences most want to fall into, so keep watching every chapter of hers for it, not just occasionally.

constructions.pattern: a short sentence opens with 'I have [verb]' as a flat, ledger-like confessional statement — a new habit, first seen in Maria's own first-person voice
constructions.example: I have checked. I have turned the arithmetic of that every way it will go. I have tried the sentence several ways and none of them let me off.
constructions.note: New in ch. 17, Maria's first chapter as narrator — five instances, all in the two interior reckoning paragraphs (the prayer, the Vail wound, the register). Distinct from the retired i-have-learned-aphorism: no general rule gets stated, each one is a flat personal fact standing on its own, closer to a confession she's logging than an observation about how the world works. Reads as earned characterisation right now — her guilt literalised as bookkeeping — but five in one chapter is enough to flag. Watch ch. 18-19 for whether it keeps recurring at this rate; if so, it wants evolving (vary the opener, or let a later chapter withhold it deliberately) rather than repeating as a default confessional tic.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: Ch. 15 and ch. 16 both avoid it. Ch. 16 ends on a bare image — daylight through the gap in the Callow Ford roof, mid-slide, no resolving line and nothing stated about what it means — which is the chapter's own outline requirement (no lucid interval, no final clarity) as much as it is this ledger's preference. Three chapters (12-14) still the longest run on this pattern; neither ch. 15 nor ch. 16 is added to the chapters list. Ch. 17 also avoids it: ends on Maria's hand on Lloyd's chest and the plain fact of feeling him believe her, not on any statement of what the moment meant. Four chapters clean running into Act III.

closers.pattern: chapter ends on an image of something indifferent or inanimate personified as 'patient', waiting out time without hurry
closers.example: the night came down slow over the burnt manse... patient, working at the dark the way it works at everything, given enough time and no one to tell it to stop
closers.note: Spent at ch. 08-09 review; stayed spent through ch. 13. Do not return to 'patient' as a chapter-ending word.
